hero.headline: Kane Williamson retires from international cricket during England series
hero.body:
Kane Williamson, New Zealand's all-time leading run scorer, has announced his retirement from international cricket with immediate effect. The announcement came during an ongoing Test series against England, bringing to an end a 16-year career that established him as one of the most successful batsmen in cricket history.

Williamson served as New Zealand captain across all formats and became the cornerstone of the national team's batting lineup. His retirement marks a significant moment for New Zealand cricket, as the country loses its most prolific run scorer. The decision to step down immediately, rather than completing the current England series, indicates the timing was driven by personal choice rather than external circumstances.

Among Williamson's major achievements was captaining New Zealand to victory in the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. This success represented a landmark moment for the team and cemented his legacy as a leader who elevated New Zealand's standing in world cricket. His consistent performances and measured approach earned him respect across the sport.

Speaking about his decision, Williamson stated: "I've given it my all in every match." This simple statement reflects the dedication he brought to international cricket throughout his career. His batting technique and consistency made him one of the most accomplished players in the modern game.

New Zealand now faces the challenge of rebuilding their batting order without their most dependable run scorer. The team is currently engaged in the Test series with England, and selectors will need to identify players capable of filling the significant void left by Williamson's departure. This transition comes at a time when experienced players have been stepping away from international cricket at an increasing rate.

Williamson's contributions to New Zealand cricket extend well beyond his statistical achievements. He helped shape the team's approach to international cricket and guided them through multiple world tournaments across all three formats. His calm leadership during high-pressure matches became a defining characteristic of his captaincy.

The immediate nature of his retirement, rather than finishing the current series, suggests Williamson felt the timing was right to step aside now. His decision allows him to move forward while still at the peak of his abilities, rather than waiting for a natural break in the schedule.

The loss of such a prolific batsman represents a significant change for New Zealand cricket. Williamson's record as the country's all-time leading run scorer stands as a testament to his longevity and consistency at the international level. As New Zealand prepares for a future without their greatest batsman, the team faces the task of developing new talent to maintain their competitive position in world cricket.

cards.headline: Trump Claims Iran Peace Deal Near as Tehran Says Nothing Finalized
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran "has been largely negotiated" following conversations with Pakistani mediators, Gulf allies, and Israeli leadership. Trump posted on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still being worked out but would be announced soon. He stated that opening the Strait of Hormuz would be part of the deal.

"An agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries," Trump wrote.

Iran's response contradicted the president's optimism. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said that while large parts of the agreement text had been finalized, Iran would not compromise on its red lines. The Fars news agency, close to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, reported that management of the Strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control, describing Trump's assertion that a deal was nearly final as "inconsistent with reality."

The announcement followed calls between Trump and leaders of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Pakistan, and Israel. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the two countries "very soon."

According to reporting by Reuters and other outlets, a revised proposal submitted by Iran and Pakistan to the United States would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension. Iran would be able to sell oil freely, and negotiations would address its nuclear program. In exchange, the U.S. would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. The agreement could potentially release 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets overseas, with nuclear discussions to occur within 30 to 60 days.

The potential deal would formally declare an end to the war that began in February and stop fighting in both Iran and Lebanon, according to regional sources cited by news agencies.

Trump's announcement came after Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated during a visit to India that "news" might arrive soon. Trump said he had met with American negotiators including special envoy Steve Witkoff, adviser Jared Kushner, and JD Vance to discuss the latest proposals.

The announcement triggered criticism from Republican hawks opposed to any agreement. Mike Pompeo, who served as CIA director and secretary of state during Trump's first term, criticized the rumored terms as too similar to the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated under the Obama administration, which Trump withdrew from in 2018.

The gap between Trump's optimistic statements and Iran's cautious response highlights significant uncertainty about whether negotiations will produce a signed agreement.

cards.headline: Shipping companies weigh costly decision as 500 vessels remain stranded in Persian Gulf
cards.teaser: More than 500 ships remain stuck in the Persian Gulf as shipping companies face mounting pressure over whether to risk passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Shipping companies and sailors face growing pressure as hundreds of vessels remain stranded in the Persian Gulf awaiting safe passage. The backlog has created a difficult dilemma for shipowners who must decide whether to wait for a resolution or attempt transit through uncertain conditions.

The situation has created significant financial strain on the maritime industry. Each day of delay adds costs for companies and crew members alike. The strait normally handles a substantial portion of global maritime traffic, making the disruption a major concern for international trade and supply chains.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes Spark Fuel Crisis in Russian-Held Crimea
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drone attacks on fuel supplies have left gas stations running dry across the occupied peninsula.
cards.body:
Ukraine has launched drone strikes targeting fuel infrastructure in Crimea, causing widespread shortages of gasoline and diesel across the Russian-held peninsula. Multiple nights of attacks have disrupted supply lines, leaving fuel stations unable to serve customers.

The strikes mark an escalation in Ukraine's campaign against occupied territories. Russian regional leaders have moved to address public concerns about the deepening fuel shortage, which has affected daily life in Crimea.

cards.headline: SpaceX set to begin trading after raising $75 billion in record public offering
cards.teaser: SpaceX is launching the largest initial public offering in history, with the company raising $75 billion ahead of its market debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX completed a $75 billion capital raise ahead of its first day of trading on public stock markets. The offering represents the largest initial public offering ever recorded, surpassing previous records for market debuts. The public sale is expected to make Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.

Investors awaited the opening of trading for SpaceX stock as the company prepared to ring the opening bell. Wall Street analysts say the debut could disrupt traditional market patterns given the unprecedented size of the offering. The space transportation company's valuation has drawn intense interest from institutional and retail investors.

cards.headline: Federal judge orders Trump administration to resume asylum processing
cards.teaser: A judge said the Department of Homeland Security unlawfully paused immigration applications after a shooting.
cards.body:
U.S. District Judge John McConnell ruled last week that the Department of Homeland Security violated the law by pausing immigration processing for nationals following a deadly shooting on National Guard officers. The judge ordered the administration to immediately resume processing applications.

McConnell criticized the Trump administration for ignoring his ruling. The pause in asylum processing came in response to the attack, but the judge found the government lacked legal authority to implement the blanket suspension of immigration applications.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo reaches 676 cases
cards.teaser: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has climbed to 676 as outbreak response efforts continue.
cards.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 676 confirmed cases, according to health authorities tracking the disease's spread. Response efforts to contain the outbreak are still working to match the pace of new infections.

The situation has drawn international attention as the United States moves to implement measures aimed at isolating itself from potential exposure.

cards.headline: European Union Migration Overhaul Takes Effect Amid Skepticism
cards.teaser: New EU rules on asylum and migration became active Friday, though doubts remain about their real-world impact.
cards.body:
The European Union implemented sweeping changes to its migration and asylum system Friday, toughening border procedures and standardizing how member states process asylum claims. The overhaul represents the bloc's most significant reform of migration policy in years, aiming to manage flows more effectively while addressing concerns from member states.

Questions persist about whether the new framework will meaningfully change outcomes on the ground. Critics have expressed skepticism that the rules will resolve longstanding disputes among EU countries over burden-sharing and border management. The changes come as migration remains a contentious political issue across Europe.

cards.headline: China Accuses Foreign Agencies of Using Spy Animals in Waters
cards.teaser: Beijing claims intelligence services have deployed equipped turtles and fish to gather sensitive maritime data.
cards.body:
China's Ministry of State Security warned Friday that foreign intelligence agencies have been using spy turtles and spy fish to monitor Chinese waters and collect sensitive maritime information. The ministry said the animals have been equipped with surveillance technology to study coastlines and gather data on naval activities.

Beijing described the alleged espionage as a threat to national security and called for increased vigilance along its maritime borders. The claims come amid broader tensions over territorial disputes and military activity in waters around China. The ministry did not provide specific evidence or name which countries it believes are responsible for the alleged operations.

cards.headline: Trump Anime Posts Strain Diplomatic Ties with Japan
cards.teaser: The president's use of anime imagery online has drawn criticism from Japanese creators and officials.
cards.body:
President Trump's repeated use of anime imagery in social media posts has created friction in diplomatic relations with Japan. The practice has drawn pushback from Japanese government officials, as well as anime creators and fans who object to the unauthorized appropriation of their cultural products for political messaging.

Japanese officials have expressed concern about the posts, which they view as disrespectful to the nation's creative industries. The controversy has added an unexpected dimension to US-Japan relations, as Tokyo navigates how to address the issue without causing broader diplomatic damage. Creators have criticized the use of their work without permission or proper context.

cards.headline: Air India Crash Investigation Shows Progress One Year Later
cards.teaser: Authorities say they have made significant advances in probing the disaster that killed 260 people.
cards.body:
Investigators marked one year since the Air India crash that killed 260 people by releasing a statement Friday confirming that significant progress has been made in the investigation.

Family members of victims gathered at the crash site to remember their loved ones through vigils and prayers, carrying portraits of those lost in the disaster, which remains among the deadliest aviation accidents in recent years.

cards.headline: World Cup Ticket Prices Spark Protests in Mexico City
cards.teaser: Teachers unions and other groups demonstrated over costs ahead of the tournament's opening match.
cards.body:
Mexico opened the World Cup with a dramatic 3-1 victory over South Africa at the packed Azteca Stadium in Mexico City, though the match was overshadowed by weeks of protests over ticket affordability. Teachers unions and other groups staged demonstrations, arguing that admission costs put matches out of reach for ordinary residents and raising broader concerns about pay and pensions.

The situation reflects tensions inherent in hosting major international sporting events in cities where portions of the population face economic strain. While organizers set prices to meet international demand, local advocates contend that residents of host cities deserve affordable access to matches played in their own stadiums.

hero.headline: Warehouse fire in Tracy continues to burn as crews work to contain blaze
hero.body:
A massive fire at a distribution warehouse in Tracy, California, continued burning Friday as firefighters battled to contain the blaze at the one million square foot Medline Industries facility. The fire ignited Thursday afternoon and spread across the street into a nearby FedEx facility, though crews were able to block further expansion, according to South San Joaquin County Fire Authority Chief Randall Bradley.

The warehouse complex, located in an industrial park about 55 miles east of San Francisco, also houses fulfillment and distribution centers for Amazon, Home Depot, and FedEx. Authorities evacuated surrounding facilities as a precaution, with officials particularly concerned about wind conditions that heightened the risk of spreading embers. However, no homes required evacuation by early Friday morning.

The inferno produced thick black smoke visible in billowing clouds from aerial images, with flames and a red hot glow visible beneath the structure. Medline, a major supplier of latex gloves, masks, surgical instruments and other medical supplies, confirmed that all employees and personnel at the site were accounted for. A company spokesperson stated: "We are coordinating closely with local authorities and first responders as we assess the fire's impact and will share more details as they become available."

Firefighters faced significant obstacles during the response. Fire Chief Bradley identified a broken sprinkler system and low water pressure in hydrants at the facility as hindering efforts to fight the blaze. These issues stemmed from the warehouse's water system rather than the city's infrastructure. Environmental conditions also worsened the situation, with low humidity, high temperatures, and strong winds exacerbating the fire's spread.

Air quality emerged as a growing concern for residents across the region. Tracy Mayor Dan Arriola said officials were evaluating air quality and potential impacts to area residents as thick smoke blanketed the surrounding area. The fire added to existing air quality challenges in the San Joaquin Valley, where residents were already contending with triple-digit temperatures.

Firefighters indicated they expected to remain on scene for an extended period to fully extinguish hot spots and prevent the fire from reigniting. The scale of the warehouse and the intensity of the blaze required substantial deployment of firefighting resources from multiple agencies across the region.

No injuries have been reported in connection with the fire. Authorities have initiated an investigation into the cause of the blaze, though results remain pending. Medline's Tracy facility served as a key distribution hub for the company's operations in Northern California, supplying medical and surgical products to healthcare providers throughout the region.

cards.headline: Federal authorities investigate vandalism on National Mall
cards.teaser: Large markings reading 8647 appeared on the grass of the National Mall, prompting a federal investigation.
cards.body:
Federal authorities opened an investigation after large markings reading 8647 were discovered etched into the grass on the National Mall in Washington. The numbers, which appeared as massive stains visible from aerial views, prompted response from law enforcement officials responsible for the historic grounds.

The numbers 8647 signify opposition to President Trump, representing a call to use the 86th Congress to remove the 47th president. The vandalism affected a significant portion of the Mall's lawn, requiring investigation into how the markings were created and who was responsible for damaging the federal property.

cards.headline: Senate leader discusses artificial intelligence policy priorities
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer outlined his agenda for artificial intelligence legislation in a new interview.
cards.body:
Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer discussed his priorities for artificial intelligence policy during recent conversations with reporters. The New York Democrat has been working to develop a legislative framework for regulating AI technologies as the sector continues to expand rapidly.

Schumer's remarks come as Congress faces pressure to address the growing influence of artificial intelligence across multiple sectors of the economy. Lawmakers have been considering various approaches to oversight and regulation, balancing innovation concerns with calls for safeguards around the technology's deployment and use.

cards.headline: British artist David Hockney dies at 88
cards.teaser: David Hockney, considered one of Britain's most important and influential artists, has died.
cards.body:
David Hockney, the iconic British painter who revolutionized 20th-century art, has died aged 88. The Bradford-born artist rose to prominence as a pop artist in the 1960s and became known for his distinctive paintings of California swimming pools, including celebrated works like "A Bigger Splash" and "Portrait of an Artist (Pool With Two Figures)." These sun-soaked depictions helped define the Los Angeles aesthetic and explored themes of love, desire, and loss.

Hockney's innovative approach to painting secured his status as one of Britain's greatest artists and a major figure in contemporary art. His influence extended across multiple artistic mediums throughout his career, inspiring generations of artists and earning him a place in major museums worldwide.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift inducted into Songwriters Hall of Fame
cards.teaser: The singer became the youngest woman inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame during a ceremony Thursday night.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift became the youngest woman inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, delivering an emotional 21-minute acceptance speech at the ceremony. During her address, she thanked her family and reflected on her songwriting career.

The honor recognizes Swift's significant contributions to popular music and her lasting impact on the industry as a songwriter.

cards.headline: Canada prepares to host World Cup opener against Bosnia-Herzegovina
cards.teaser: The host nation faces Bosnia-Herzegovina as the 2026 World Cup begins, with soccer participation surpassing hockey among Canadian youth.
cards.body:
Canada is set to kick off the World Cup against Bosnia-Herzegovina in a historic moment for the nation's soccer ambitions. Coach Jesse Marsch expressed confidence in his team's momentum heading into the match, citing growing enthusiasm surrounding the tournament.

The World Cup spotlight comes as soccer undergoes a dramatic surge in popularity across Canada. According to a report by Jumpstart, a Canadian charity, soccer has now surpassed hockey as the leading sport among youth participants, reflecting a significant shift in the country's athletic landscape and signaling soccer's rising prominence.

cards.headline: Bollywood performer to sing at World Cup opening ceremony in Toronto
cards.teaser: A Canadian-born Bollywood artist will perform her official FIFA song at the Toronto opening ceremony.
cards.body:
A Bollywood star prepared to take the stage at the World Cup opening ceremony in Toronto, where she will perform her official FIFA song. The Canadian-born artist created a unity-themed song for the tournament, which brings together nations from around the world.

The opening ceremony marks the start of the 2026 World Cup, with Canada serving as one of the host nations alongside the United States and Mexico. The performance will showcase the multicultural character of the host country as the tournament begins.

hero.headline: Oil prices drop and stocks rise as Trump says Iran peace deal nearing completion
hero.body:
President Trump announced he was cancelling additional military strikes on Iran and claimed a peace agreement could be close, triggering sharp market movements. Oil prices fell and stock indices rallied on the news, though Iran's government disputed the president's characterization of the negotiations.

Oil experienced dramatic declines following the announcement. Brent crude dropped 16% initially, while US crude fell 17.6%. By late Wednesday afternoon London time, Brent crude was down 13.5% to $94.36 a barrel, and US crude fell 15.5% to $95.36, marking its biggest single-day drop since the Covid-19 lockdowns six years ago. The price declines reflected investor relief over reduced military tensions in the Persian Gulf.

Stock markets worldwide responded positively to the ceasefire news. Wall Street recorded its biggest single-day rally in a year. The S&P 500 rallied 2.5% to 6,782.81, while the Dow Jones industrial average gained more than 1,300 points, or 2.9%, finishing at 47,909.92. The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite advanced 2.8% to 22,634.99. Asian and European markets also surged, with Japan's Nikkei 225 gaining over 5%, South Korea's Kospi soaring 7.5%, and the pan-European Stoxx 600 climbing 3.7%.

Travel and leisure stocks performed particularly well. Air France gained 13%, Lufthansa jumped 8%, British Airways owner IAG rose 8%, and holiday group Tui gained nearly 10%. However, energy company shares tumbled, with BP down 6% and Shell losing 4.7%.

The deal involved a two-week conditional ceasefire. According to Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, passage through the Strait of Hormuz would be allowed for two weeks under Iran's military management. Peace negotiations between the US and Iran were scheduled to begin in Islamabad on Friday. However, Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's claims, saying no final decision on an agreement had been reached.

Treasury yields eased following the ceasefire announcement. The yield on the 10-year US treasury fell to 4.24% from 4.30%, while the UK 10-year government bond yield dropped to 4.7% from 4.9%. Gold prices rose over 2% to $4,812 an ounce, and bitcoin advanced 2.9% to $71,327.

Despite the optimistic market reaction, analysts warned of fragility ahead. Kathleen Brooks from trading platform XTB noted that oil prices could surge back above $110 per barrel for Brent crude if bombing restarted. Jim Reid from Deutsche Bank cautioned that investors should monitor whether the ceasefire holds and whether talks could lead to sustained de-escalation.

Reports indicated that Israel launched strikes on Lebanon and that Iran halted oil tanker passage following alleged ceasefire breaches, which later nudged oil prices higher from their lows.

cards.headline: SpaceX set to begin trading after raising $75 billion in record public offering
cards.teaser: SpaceX is launching the largest initial public offering in history, with the company raising $75 billion ahead of its market debut.
cards.body:
SpaceX completed a $75 billion capital raise ahead of its first day of trading on public stock markets. The offering represents the largest initial public offering ever recorded, surpassing previous records for market debuts. The public sale is expected to make Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire.

Investors awaited the opening of trading for SpaceX stock as the company prepared to ring the opening bell. Wall Street analysts say the debut could disrupt traditional market patterns given the unprecedented size of the offering. The space transportation company's valuation has drawn intense interest from institutional and retail investors.

cards.teaser: More than 500 ships remain stuck in the Persian Gulf as shipping companies face mounting pressure over whether to risk passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Shipping companies and sailors face growing pressure as hundreds of vessels remain stranded in the Persian Gulf awaiting safe passage. The backlog has created a difficult dilemma for shipowners who must decide whether to wait for a resolution or attempt transit through uncertain conditions.

cards.headline: SpaceX president suggests potential merger with Tesla
cards.teaser: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell indicated a possible merger between SpaceX and Tesla, saying it might make Elon Musk's life easier.
cards.body:
SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell floated the possibility of a merger between SpaceX and Tesla on the day of SpaceX's public offering. Shotwell suggested the combination could simplify operations for Elon Musk, who leads both companies. The comments sparked immediate speculation among analysts and investors.

Analysts have begun debating the feasibility and implications of combining the aerospace and automotive companies. Some see overlap between the companies' operations and technologies, while others question the regulatory and operational challenges such a merger would face. The speculation heated up as SpaceX prepared to begin trading as a public company.

cards.headline: World Cup expected to drive record sports gambling activity
cards.teaser: Betting sites like FanDuel and DraftKings are counting on the World Cup to boost online sports gambling during a period of sluggish growth.
cards.body:
The World Cup is shaping up to be the largest betting event in history, driven in part by an expanded tournament schedule that will increase the total number of games played. The surge in matches is expected to generate a significant spike in betting activity.

Major online sportsbooks including FanDuel and DraftKings are preparing for heightened engagement around the tournament. At a time when the sports betting sector has experienced slower growth, companies are leveraging the World Cup as a key opportunity to attract new users and boost activity among existing customers.

cards.headline: Americans show declining financial literacy, researchers find
cards.teaser: People with poor understanding of basic finances often make bad decisions on money matters, and the problem appears to be worsening.
cards.body:
Americans lack proficiency in basic financial concepts and the trend is deteriorating, according to new research. Researchers found that individuals with limited financial knowledge frequently make poor choices about money management, saving and investing.

The findings suggest a growing gap in essential money skills among the population. Financial literacy encompasses understanding of fundamental concepts like interest rates, inflation, risk diversification and debt management. Researchers say the lack of these skills can lead to costly mistakes that affect long-term financial security.

cards.headline: S&P 500 trades lower as investors await details on Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 moved lower as traders monitored developments in Iran deal negotiations and prepared for SpaceX's market debut.
cards.body:
President Trump canceled planned strikes on Iran and signaled that a peace deal could come soon, though Iran stated the agreement hasn't been finalized yet. Oil prices fell and stocks rallied on the reduced military tensions, though broader market sentiment remained cautious as traders awaited concrete details about any potential agreement.

The S&P 500 showed mixed performance amid the uncertainty. Energy stocks saw significant activity as investors processed the implications of easing tensions. Trading also reflected anticipation surrounding SpaceX's upcoming market debut.

hero.headline: Pokémon Go player data used to train AI with military drone applications
hero.body:
Data collected from Pokémon Go players has been used to train artificial intelligence systems designed to help military drones navigate and locate themselves in war zones, raising significant privacy concerns about how gaming data is repurposed beyond its original entertainment context.

Pokémon Go, the augmented reality mobile game that launched in 2016, became a cultural phenomenon with over 800 million downloads by 2018. The game required players to physically explore real-world locations using their smartphone cameras to capture virtual creatures. In 2021, the game introduced AR Scans, a feature that rewarded players for scanning real locations with their devices. Users had to opt in to participate and voluntarily upload the recordings.

Niantic, the company that created Pokémon Go in partnership with Nintendo, collected location scan data from players before selling its gaming division to Saudi Arabian-owned Scopely for 3.5 billion US dollars in 2025. The historical scans were used to train Niantic's artificial intelligence models to recognize and interpret physical spaces. Niantic Spatial, a spin-off company from Niantic, subsequently announced a partnership with Vantor, a company specializing in spatial detection software for drones used by some militaries.

The partnership addresses a critical gap in drone operations. According to the companies' announcement, it tackles problems including GPS unavailability, spoofing, interference and jamming. The technology allows drones to navigate and coordinate precisely in areas where satellite signals are compromised or unavailable. Vantor later secured a deal with the US Army worth up to 217 million US dollars for training software.

Both Niantic Spatial and Vantor stated that ground scans from the game were not directly provided to Vantor as part of the partnership, but rather the scans were used to train Niantic's foundational AI models. A Niantic Spatial spokesperson explained that AR Scans were submitted voluntarily by players who opted into the feature and were subject to the applicable terms of service and privacy policy.

The use of civilian gaming data for military purposes has drawn criticism from privacy advocates and technology experts. Tom Sulston, head of policy at Digital Rights Watch, emphasized that most people do not read extensive legal documents when playing video games. He called for regulators to focus on tests that prioritize user interests and fairness to prevent such exploitation.

Dr Rob Nicholls, senior researcher at the University of Sydney's centre for AI, trust and governance, suggested this case represents only the beginning of similar data repurposing incidents. He noted that military fitness tracking data from apps like Strava has previously been used to identify military facility locations, prompting various militaries to restrict GPS-enabled devices.

The disclosure highlights the ongoing tension between data collection practices and user privacy expectations as artificial intelligence development accelerates and demands ever-larger training datasets.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo reaches 676 cases
cards.teaser: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has climbed to 676 as outbreak response efforts continue.
cards.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 676 confirmed cases, according to health authorities tracking the disease's spread. Response efforts to contain the outbreak are still working to match the pace of new infections.

The situation has drawn international attention as the United States moves to implement measures aimed at isolating itself from potential exposure.

cards.headline: Verizon sends customer refurbished phone with mobile device management software installed
cards.teaser: A Verizon customer received a refurbished phone with enterprise management software still active, which then remotely deleted his personal data.
cards.body:
Verizon sent a customer a refurbished phone that still had mobile device management software installed from its previous use, leading to the remote deletion of the new owner's data. The incident raises questions about the company's procedures for preparing used devices for resale to new customers.

Mobile device management software allows organizations to remotely control, configure, and wipe devices issued to employees. The presence of such software on a phone sold as refurbished suggests inadequate clearing of previous configurations before the device was returned to inventory and sent to a new customer.

cards.headline: SpaceX initial public offering set to launch Friday
cards.teaser: SpaceX is preparing to go public with an initial public offering scheduled for Friday, according to aerospace industry reports.
cards.body:
SpaceX is set to launch its initial public offering on Friday, marking a significant shift for the private space company founded by Elon Musk. The move will make shares of the rocket manufacturer and launch services provider available to public investors for the first time.

The report on the upcoming IPO appeared alongside news that Nova is progressing through its test campaign. Industry observers have been tracking developments across multiple commercial space companies as the sector continues to expand beyond traditional government-led space programs.

cards.headline: World Cup referees to use digital twins and sensor technology for video review
cards.teaser: Officials at the World Cup will use digital player replicas created from 3D body scans and sensor data to review plays from multiple angles.
cards.body:
Referees at the World Cup will employ new technology that creates digital twins of each player, allowing officials to view plays from any angle during video review. The system combines cameras, sensors, and 3D body scans to generate accurate virtual representations of player movements and positions.

The technology aims to reduce incorrect calls by giving referees more comprehensive views of contested plays than traditional camera angles provide. Digital twins can be rotated and viewed from perspectives not available through fixed stadium cameras, potentially clarifying close calls on offside positions, fouls, and other disputed plays.

cards.headline: Indian AI company Avataar launches lower-cost video generation model
cards.teaser: Avataar AI has released a video generation model designed for the Indian market, priced significantly lower than competing services.
cards.body:
Avataar AI has launched a distilled video generation model priced at $0.005 per second of generated video, making it significantly cheaper than competing AI video services. The company built the model with India's market in mind, incorporating cultural awareness and addressing local scale requirements.

The model is designed to be faster than existing alternatives while remaining affordable for Indian content creators and businesses.

cards.headline: Minecraft releases version 26.2 Release Candidate 2
cards.teaser: Minecraft has published Release Candidate 2 of version 26.2, continuing testing of new features ahead of the full update.
cards.body:
Minecraft has released version 26.2 Release Candidate 2, the latest pre-release version as the game approaches its full 26.2 update. The release candidate allows players to test features and identify bugs before the final version launches.

The 26.2 update includes changes to Hardcore mode that affect how players can interact with those worlds. Release candidates typically indicate that development is nearing completion, with the full release expected to follow after final testing confirms stability.

hero.headline: Kane Williamson retires from international cricket during England series
hero.body:
Kane Williamson, New Zealand's all-time leading run scorer, has announced his retirement from international cricket with immediate effect. The announcement came during an ongoing Test series against England, bringing to an end a 16-year career that established him as one of the most successful batsmen in cricket history.

Williamson served as New Zealand captain across all formats and became the cornerstone of the national team's batting lineup. His retirement marks a significant moment for New Zealand cricket, as the country loses its most prolific run scorer. The decision to step down immediately, rather than completing the current England series, indicates the timing was driven by personal choice rather than external circumstances.

Among Williamson's major achievements was captaining New Zealand to victory in the inaugural World Test Championship in 2021. This success represented a landmark moment for the team and cemented his legacy as a leader who elevated New Zealand's standing in world cricket. His consistent performances and measured approach earned him respect across the sport.

Speaking about his decision, Williamson stated: "I've given it my all in every match." This simple statement reflects the dedication he brought to international cricket throughout his career. His batting technique and consistency made him one of the most accomplished players in the modern game.

New Zealand now faces the challenge of rebuilding their batting order without their most dependable run scorer. The team is currently engaged in the Test series with England, and selectors will need to identify players capable of filling the significant void left by Williamson's departure. This transition comes at a time when experienced players have been stepping away from international cricket at an increasing rate.

Williamson's contributions to New Zealand cricket extend well beyond his statistical achievements. He helped shape the team's approach to international cricket and guided them through multiple world tournaments across all three formats. His calm leadership during high-pressure matches became a defining characteristic of his captaincy.

The immediate nature of his retirement, rather than finishing the current series, suggests Williamson felt the timing was right to step aside now. His decision allows him to move forward while still at the peak of his abilities, rather than waiting for a natural break in the schedule.

The loss of such a prolific batsman represents a significant change for New Zealand cricket. Williamson's record as the country's all-time leading run scorer stands as a testament to his longevity and consistency at the international level. As New Zealand prepares for a future without their greatest batsman, the team faces the task of developing new talent to maintain their competitive position in world cricket.

cards.headline: Seahawks receive Super Bowl LX championship rings
cards.teaser: The Seattle Seahawks received their Super Bowl LX championship rings in a ceremony recognizing their title victory.
cards.body:
The Seattle Seahawks held a ring ceremony to distribute Super Bowl LX championship rings to players and staff. The rings were designed by Jason of Beverly Hills and feature authentic football material along with 50 diamonds.

The celebration took place during the team's minicamp activities. The ring designs incorporate elements that recognize the franchise's fans, city, and history, marking the Seahawks' Super Bowl LX championship victory.

cards.headline: Manchester City sign England forward Beth Mead from Arsenal
cards.teaser: Manchester City confirmed the signing of England international Beth Mead on a free transfer from Arsenal.
cards.body:
Beth Mead has joined Manchester City on a free transfer after nine years at Arsenal. The 31-year-old England forward, who has scored 40 times in 81 appearances for her country, has signed a three-year deal with the Women's Super League champions.

Mead described the move as a "no-brainer," highlighting how Manchester City's playing style suits her approach to the game. She becomes City's first signing of the summer transfer window.

cards.headline: Pierre Gasly regains Monaco Grand Prix podium after successful appeal
cards.teaser: Alpine driver Pierre Gasly has been reinstated to third place at the Monaco Grand Prix after stewards rescinded two pit lane speeding penalties.
cards.body:
Pierre Gasly has been reinstated to third place at the Monaco Grand Prix after stewards rescinded two pit-lane speeding penalties. The Frenchman had originally finished third on track but was demoted to seventh following the penalties applied after the race.

Alpine successfully appealed the decision, leading Formula One officials to acknowledge a timekeeping error in their measurements. The stewards subsequently overturned the penalties, restoring Gasly to the podium.

cards.headline: George Russell tops first practice at Barcelona Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Mercedes driver George Russell set the fastest time in first practice for the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix.
cards.body:
George Russell posted the fastest time in the opening practice session at the Barcelona-Catalunya circuit, edging out McLaren's Oscar Piastri. The Mercedes driver set the pace in Friday morning's first practice as teams began their weekend preparations.

The session allowed competitors to evaluate performance on the Spanish track and make initial setup adjustments ahead of the qualifying and race weekend.

cards.headline: College World Series features top MLB draft prospects
cards.teaser: The 2026 Men's College World Series in Omaha showcases several players expected to be selected in the upcoming MLB draft.
cards.body:
Eight teams are competing in the College World Series, with multiple players projected as high MLB draft picks. Scouts and executives are evaluating talent throughout the tournament as the draft approaches.

The tournament field includes teams with varying strengths and weaknesses. Opposing coaches have analyzed each squad's capabilities ahead of the championship rounds. The College World Series serves as a final showcase for draft-eligible players to demonstrate their skills against top competition before professional teams make their selections.

cards.headline: Republic of Ireland to host Israel at neutral venue in Nations League
cards.teaser: The Football Association of Ireland confirmed the home Nations League match against Israel will be played at a neutral location.
cards.body:
The Football Association of Ireland has confirmed that the Republic of Ireland's home Nations League fixture against Israel will be held at a neutral venue rather than at the Aviva Stadium. The match had been scheduled for 4 October.

The decision follows widespread protests from Irish players, fans and celebrities calling for a boycott of the game over the Palestinian death toll in the Gaza war. The fixture will be played behind closed doors at the neutral venue.

hero.headline: British artist David Hockney dies at 88
hero.body:
David Hockney, the iconic British painter whose revolutionary work shaped contemporary art across seven decades, has died peacefully at home aged 88. His death on June 11, 2026, marks the loss of one of the most important figures in modern and contemporary art.

Hockney rose to prominence during the 1960s as a leading pop artist, becoming best known for his paintings of California swimming pools that helped define the Los Angeles aesthetic. Works such as "A Bigger Splash" and "Portrait of an Artist (Pool With Two Figures)" depicted scenes of love, lust and loss unfolding beneath sun-soaked skies. These paintings brought him international recognition and made him one of the most recognizable artists of his generation.

Born in Bradford, West Yorkshire, in 1937, Hockney came from what he described as a "radical working-class family" whose parents nurtured his artistic talents. He studied art at Bradford College before enrolling at London's Royal College of Art in 1959, where he quickly developed a reputation as a uniquely talented but rebellious figure. His refusal to conform to traditional requirements nearly prevented his graduation, but the college recognized his exceptional abilities and awarded him his diploma.

Hockney's willingness to challenge conventions extended throughout his career. His early works openly depicted gay life and relationships with honesty and openness at a time when homosexuality remained illegal in Britain. With his distinctive bleach-blonde hair and thick-rimmed spectacles, he became a prominent figure in the vibrant social scenes of 1960s London and America.

After relocating to Los Angeles in the mid-1960s, Hockney's work evolved toward a more mature and restrained style while maintaining its emotional depth. His paintings gained acclaim for their ability to convey complex feelings about love and loss. In November 2018, his masterpiece "Portrait of an Artist (Pool With Two Figures)" sold for 90.3 million dollars at auction, setting a world record for a living artist at that time.

Throughout his career, Hockney continuously reinvented himself. He created stage designs for opera, experimented with photo collages, and in later years explored digital media and iPad painting to create large-scale landscapes. Even after suffering a stroke in 2012, he remained remarkably productive.

The artist maintained studios in London, Los Angeles, and Normandy, France. He received the Order of Merit from Queen Elizabeth II in 2012, one of Britain's highest civilian awards. His 2012 Royal Academy exhibition attracted over 600,000 visitors, making it one of the institution's most attended shows.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Hockney's "vivid, instantly recognisable work influenced generations of artists." The Tate Gallery described him as an "endlessly inventive artist" whose loss represents an immense blow to the art world. The institution plans major retrospective exhibitions next year, ensuring his extraordinary legacy continues to inspire viewers worldwide.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift inducted into Songwriters Hall of Fame
cards.teaser: Steven Spielberg introduced the singer as the youngest female inductee to the Hall of Fame.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift became the youngest woman ever inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame at the organization's annual ceremony. Director Steven Spielberg introduced her, praising Swift as someone unafraid of shattering records as a writer, singer, and storyteller. He compared her songwriting to the legendary Lennon-McCartney partnership.

Musical artist Sombr performed covers of two Swift songs during the event. The Songwriters Hall of Fame ceremony brings together performers, songwriters, and music industry figures to celebrate contributions to songwriting.

cards.headline: Netflix renews House of Guinness for second season
cards.teaser: The period drama about the Irish brewing family will begin production in early 2027.
cards.body:
Netflix has greenlit a second season of House of Guinness, the period drama created by Stephen Knight about the famous Irish brewing family. Production on the new season is scheduled to begin in early 2027.

The show dramatizes the history of the Guinness family and their brewing empire. Knight, known for creating Peaky Blinders, developed the series for Netflix. The streaming service declined to comment on the renewal, which was confirmed by industry sources.

cards.headline: Children of serial killer Richard Kuklinski speak publicly
cards.teaser: The offspring of the man known as The Iceman say they have been hounded by fans of their father.
cards.body:
The children of Richard Kuklinski, known as The Iceman, have spoken publicly about the impact of their father's notoriety. They describe being pursued and harassed by true crime enthusiasts who idolize their father, viewing him as an icon worthy of celebration.

The family rejects this romanticization of Kuklinski's crimes. They say the explosion of true crime media in recent years has intensified unwanted attention on their lives, forcing them to confront their father's legacy and the public's fascination with serial killers.

cards.headline: Noah Wyle and Sally Field discuss reunion on The Pitt
cards.teaser: The actors, who previously worked together on ER, appear in a new medical drama series.
cards.body:
Noah Wyle and Sally Field discussed their work on The Pitt, a new medical drama, in an interview for the Actors on Actors series. The two previously worked together on ER, where Wyle was a breakout star and Field was already an established performer with an Oscar to her name.

Field reflected on the shift in television's prestige during her career, noting it was a big gamble once for an Oscar winner to do TV. Wyle and Field spoke about the physical demands of shooting the medical drama, mentioning exhaustion from production and working with CGI elements. The full interview appears on CNN and Variety's YouTube channel.

cards.headline: Brazilian player wins Candy Crush world championship
cards.teaser: Luana from Bahia, Brazil took first place in the game's All Stars tournament.
cards.body:
Luana, an art student from Bahia, Brazil, won the 2026 Candy Crush All Stars world championship. She competed against millions of players from 25 countries in remote qualifying rounds before reaching the live final.

The tournament culminated in a live event where Luana secured victory in the final game. The 2026 competition was the largest in the tournament's history, with more participants and countries represented than in previous years. King, the game's publisher, organizes the annual championship for Candy Crush players worldwide.

cards.headline: Fruit Bats releases full-band album The Landfill
cards.teaser: Musician Eric D. Johnson explores human stories on a record recorded with live energy.
cards.body:
Fruit Bats, the musical project led by Eric D. Johnson, released a new full-band album titled The Landfill. The record features songs that explore everyday human experiences and was recorded with a live band rather than as a solo or studio-heavy production.

Johnson wrote material for the album that examines what he describes as the unglamorous bits that make up the human story. The album showcases a different approach than some of Fruit Bats' previous work, emphasizing the energy of live performance in the recording process.

hero.headline: Senator Schiff questions Trump's account of Iran war negotiations
hero.body:
Senator Adam Schiff of California said President Trump's statements about negotiations to end the conflict with Iran lack credibility. The Democratic senator made his remarks after a day in which Trump first threatened increased military strikes on Tehran, then reversed course by canceling the planned attacks.

Trump claimed that Iran's supreme leader had approved a deal to reopen negotiations, but Schiff disputed this assertion. Iran's foreign ministry rejected Trump's claims, with a spokesperson stating that large parts of the negotiation text had been finalized but that Iran would not compromise on its core demands. The semi-official Iranian news agency Tasnim said that "until a potential understanding is announced by Iran, any news from Trump on this matter should be dismissed."

"Trump is telling falsehood after falsehood about the state of negotiations," Schiff said, characterizing the president's account as lacking credibility. The senator's statement reflects broader Democratic concerns about the reliability of information coming from the White House regarding military operations and diplomatic efforts.

The back-and-forth between Trump and Iran underscores the uncertainty surrounding the path forward in the conflict. Trump's pattern of announcing then withdrawing military plans has raised questions among lawmakers about the administration's strategy. The president has not provided details about the alleged agreement with Iran's leadership or what concessions either side may have made.

Two days of escalating attacks between the nations had created heightened tensions before Trump announced the cancellation of further strikes. His repeated claims about imminent deals, which Iran has consistently contradicted, have added confusion about the actual state of negotiations.

The dispute between the White House and congressional Democrats over the accuracy of Trump's Iran statements reflects the strained relationship between the administration and the Democratic opposition. Schiff, who serves on committees with oversight responsibilities for intelligence and foreign policy matters, has been a frequent critic of the president's handling of foreign policy and military decisions.

Trump's sudden reversals on military action have not been confined to Iran. His approach to using force and announcing diplomatic breakthroughs, only to change course, has become a pattern that concerns both Democrats and some Republicans in Congress who have questioned whether the administration has a coherent strategy.

The incident highlights broader questions about communication from the White House on matters of national security and military operations. Lawmakers across both parties have expressed frustration about receiving mixed signals on major foreign policy decisions, particularly regarding when military action will be taken and what diplomatic progress has actually been achieved.

cards.headline: Federal judge orders Trump administration to resume asylum processing
cards.teaser: A judge said the Department of Homeland Security unlawfully paused immigration applications after a shooting.
cards.body:
U.S. District Judge John McConnell ruled last week that the Department of Homeland Security violated the law by pausing immigration processing for nationals following a deadly shooting on National Guard officers. The judge ordered the administration to immediately resume processing applications.

McConnell criticized the Trump administration for ignoring his ruling. The pause in asylum processing came in response to the attack, but the judge found the government lacked legal authority to implement the blanket suspension of immigration applications.

cards.headline: White House releases UFO videos and government records
cards.teaser: The Trump administration disclosed documents showing years of government monitoring of unexplained aerial phenomena.
cards.body:
The Trump administration released a collection of government records and videos showing orb-like objects moving across the sky. The disclosure includes documentation of suspected unidentified aerial phenomena that government agents have monitored and investigated over multiple years.

The release aims to provide transparency about government examination of such sightings, which have been the subject of conspiracy theories. The documents show that officials have spent years documenting incidents involving objects that appear to move in ways not easily explained by conventional aircraft.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio compares UFC to moon landing
cards.teaser: Marco Rubio drew parallels between mixed martial arts and America's 1969 lunar mission ahead of a White House event.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio compared UFC to the 1969 moon landing ahead of the UFC Freedom 250 event scheduled at the White House. Rubio referenced President Kennedy's announcement about putting a man on the moon and returning him safely to Earth.

The comparison came as the administration prepares to host the UFC event at the White House on Sunday. Rubio suggested both represented ambitious American achievements that some doubted were possible.

cards.headline: Texas attorney general warns Big 12 over potential quarterback sanctions
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton threatened legal action if schools penalize Texas Tech for playing a quarterback who sued the NCAA.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sent a letter to Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark and conference schools warning of potential legal action if Texas Tech faces sanctions over its decision to play quarterback Behren Morton, who sued to regain eligibility.

Paxton, a Republican candidate for governor, indicated the state would consider suing any Big 12 institution that penalizes Texas Tech for fielding the quarterback despite potential conference consequences.

cards.headline: Most Americans say country's best days are behind it as 250th birthday approaches
cards.teaser: A Pew Research Center analysis found national pessimism despite personal hopefulness about the future.
cards.body:
Nearly seven in 10 U.S. adults expressed dissatisfaction with the country's direction in January 2026, according to Pew Research Center, with only 29 percent saying they were satisfied as the nation approaches its 250th birthday.

The pessimism reflects broader frustrations among Americans. Nearly 80 percent of consumers experienced product or service problems in 2025, with about two-thirds reporting intense anger over the issues, according to a National Consumer Rage survey. Many feel trapped in a cycle of overcharges, poor customer service, faulty products and billing errors—compounded by soaring prices and rising inflation.

cards.headline: Defense attorneys ask judge to investigate prosecutors in Tyler Robinson case
cards.teaser: Robinson's lawyers requested an investigation into whether prosecutors violated a gag order with media comments.
cards.body:
Tyler Robinson's attorneys asked Judge Tony Graf to investigate comments made by prosecutors to TMZ and Fox News. The defense team raised concerns that the statements may have violated a gag order in the case.

The request for an investigation centers on whether prosecutors improperly discussed case details with media outlets. Judge Graf has not yet ruled on the defense motion.
